course.title: AP Precalculus
course.description: Build the function toolkit that calculus depends on: how quantities change together, polynomial and rational functions, exponential and logarithmic models, and trigonometric and polar functions.
course.previewDescription: Study how outputs change with inputs, then use polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions to describe patterns and build models.

unit.title: Polynomial and Rational Functions

topic.title: Polynomial Functions and End Behavior
topic.summary: Limit notation, why the leading term controls the far left and far right of the graph, and the four end-behavior cases.

questions.prompt: Let g(x) = −3x⁵ + 2x. What is the value of lim x→−∞ g(x)?
questions.explanation: The leading term is −3x⁵, which has odd degree and a negative coefficient. For large negative x, x⁵ is very negative, so −3x⁵ is very positive. The outputs increase without bound.
choiceExplanations: A negative number to the fifth power is negative, and the leading coefficient −3 flips it to positive, so outputs increase without bound.
−∞ is the behavior as x → ∞, not as x → −∞.
Outputs do not settle on 0. A polynomial of degree 5 grows without bound at both ends.
−3 is the leading coefficient, not a limit of the outputs.
questions.distinguisher: On the left end of an odd-degree polynomial, the sign is the opposite of the right end.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes the end behavior of f(x) = 2x⁴ − x³ + 7?
choices: The left end falls and the right end rises.
Both ends rise.
Both ends fall.
The left end rises and the right end falls.
questions.explanation: The leading term is 2x⁴, which has even degree and a positive coefficient. Both ends rise.
choiceExplanations: This is the pattern of an odd-degree polynomial with a positive leading coefficient, not an even-degree one.
Even degree makes the ends match, and the positive leading coefficient makes them rise.
Both ends would fall only if the leading coefficient were negative.
This is the pattern of an odd-degree polynomial with a negative leading coefficient.
questions.distinguisher: Even degree means the ends match. The sign of the leading coefficient picks up or down.

questions.prompt: Which polynomial function has a graph that falls to the left and rises to the right?
choices: f(x) = −x³ + 2
f(x) = x⁴ − 4
f(x) = −x⁴ + 3x
f(x) = x³ − 4x
questions.explanation: Falling left and rising right needs odd degree with a positive leading coefficient. Only x³ − 4x fits.
choiceExplanations: The degree is odd, but the negative coefficient reverses the direction: it rises on the left and falls on the right.
Even degree gives ends that match, so both ends would rise.
Even degree gives ends that match, so both ends would fall.
Odd degree gives opposite ends, and the positive coefficient sends the right end up.
questions.distinguisher: Odd degree with a positive leading coefficient is the only combination that falls left and rises right.

questions.prompt: Which part of a polynomial determines its end behavior?
choices: Its constant term, which is the y-intercept
Its degree alone, without regard to any coefficient
Its leading term, because it dominates for inputs far from zero
Its zero closest to the origin
questions.explanation: For large inputs the highest power outgrows every other term, so the leading term decides the end behavior.
choiceExplanations: The constant term shifts the graph vertically but does not matter for the far ends.
The degree decides whether the ends match, but the sign of the leading coefficient is also needed to know which way they point.
The leading term is far larger than the rest for inputs far from zero, so it controls the ends.
Zeros are in the middle of the graph. They do not affect the far ends.
questions.distinguisher: The degree is only half of the story. The sign of the leading coefficient finishes it.

questions.prompt: The table shows terms of p(x) = x³ − 100x². Which conclusion is best supported?
choices: The function p is negative for every input, because of the −100x² term.
For large inputs, p behaves like x³, because x³ becomes far larger than 100x².
For large inputs, p behaves like −100x², because its coefficient has the larger size.
The function p is zero for large inputs, because the terms cancel at x = 100.
questions.explanation: At x = 10 the polynomial is negative, but by x = 10,000 it is about 99% of x³. The leading term takes over as x grows.
choiceExplanations: p(10) is negative, but p(1,000) and p(10,000) are positive, so p is not negative everywhere.
The ratio of x³ to 100x² grows without bound, so for large inputs x³ controls the output.
A large coefficient helps at small inputs, but a higher power eventually beats any coefficient.
The cancellation at x = 100 is a single input. After that the outputs are positive.
questions.distinguisher: A higher power eventually beats a larger coefficient on a lower power.

questions.prompt: Which statement is equivalent to lim x→−∞ f(x) = −∞?
choices: As inputs increase without bound, outputs decrease without bound.
The function f has an output equal to −∞ at x = 0.
The graph of f falls only to the left of the y-axis.
As inputs decrease without bound, outputs decrease without bound.
questions.explanation: The notation x → −∞ means the input decreases without bound, and f(x) = −∞ means the outputs decrease without bound too.
choiceExplanations: This describes x → ∞, the right end, not x → −∞, the left end.
∞ is not a number the function takes as an output, and the statement is about the far left, not x = 0.
The statement is about the far left end, not just the left side of the y-axis, and says nothing about the rest of the graph.
The limit describes what happens to outputs as inputs decrease without bound, which is the far left end.
questions.distinguisher: The input direction is written under the limit. The output direction follows the equals sign.

questions.prompt: A polynomial p has odd degree and a negative leading coefficient. Which pair of limits describes its end behavior?
choices: lim x→−∞ p(x) = −∞ and lim x→∞ p(x) = ∞
lim x→−∞ p(x) = −∞ and lim x→∞ p(x) = −∞
lim x→−∞ p(x) = ∞ and lim x→∞ p(x) = −∞
lim x→−∞ p(x) = ∞ and lim x→∞ p(x) = ∞
questions.explanation: Odd degree means the ends go in opposite directions. A negative leading coefficient makes the right end fall, so the left end rises.
choiceExplanations: This is odd degree with a positive leading coefficient. The ends are opposite, but the directions are reversed.
Both ends falling happens for even degree with a negative coefficient, not odd degree.
Odd degree gives opposite ends, and a negative leading coefficient makes the right end fall, so the left end rises.
Both ends rising happens for even degree with a positive coefficient, not odd degree.
questions.distinguisher: Start from the right end: a negative coefficient sends it down, and odd degree sends the left end the other way.

questions.prompt: The graph of a polynomial rises without bound at the far left and rises without bound at the far right. Which function could it be?
choices: p(x) = 3x⁴ − 5x² + 1
p(x) = x³ − x
p(x) = −2x⁴ + x
p(x) = −x⁵ + 2x
questions.explanation: Both ends rise, so the degree is even and the leading coefficient is positive. Only 3x⁴ − 5x² + 1 matches.
choiceExplanations: Even degree and a positive leading coefficient give two ends that both rise.
The leading coefficient is positive, but the degree is odd, so the left end falls.
The degree is even, but the negative coefficient makes both ends fall.
The degree is odd and the coefficient is negative, so the left end rises and the right end falls.
questions.distinguisher: A positive leading coefficient is not enough. The degree must be even for both ends to rise.

questions.prompt: Let f(x) = x⁴ and g(x) = 1000x³. For very large positive inputs, which function has the greater output?
choices: g, because its coefficient 1000 is larger than 1
They are equal, because both are polynomials
f, because a higher power eventually beats a larger coefficient
g, because its graph is steeper near x = 1
questions.explanation: Beyond x = 1000, x⁴ is larger than 1000x³, because x⁴ = x · x³ and x > 1000. A higher power wins for large inputs.
choiceExplanations: A large coefficient helps only for small inputs. The power matters more as x grows.
Being polynomials does not make their outputs equal. They have different degrees and different growth.
x⁴ = x · x³, so once x exceeds 1000 the function f outgrows 1000x³ and stays ahead.
Steepness near x = 1 is irrelevant. The question asks about very large inputs.
questions.distinguisher: Compare degrees first. Coefficients matter only between functions of the same degree.

questions.prompt: A polynomial p satisfies lim x→∞ p(x) = −∞ and lim x→−∞ p(x) = −∞. Which statement must be true?
choices: The degree of p is odd and the leading coefficient is negative.
The degree of p is even and the leading coefficient is positive.
The degree of p is odd and the leading coefficient is positive.
The degree of p is even and the leading coefficient is negative.
questions.explanation: The two ends point the same direction, so the degree is even. Both ends fall, so the leading coefficient is negative.
choiceExplanations: An odd degree sends the two ends in opposite directions, so it cannot give two falling ends.
A positive leading coefficient with even degree makes both ends rise, not fall.
An odd degree sends the ends in opposite directions, so it cannot match this behavior.
Matching ends mean even degree, and both falling means a negative leading coefficient.
questions.distinguisher: Matching ends decide the parity. Their direction decides the sign.
